stem:
In a class in Kochi, Meera and Arjun list four activities. In which activities does the observation show that matter is made of extremely small particles and does not become nothing?

| activity | W | X | Y | Z |
| activity | grinding a piece of chalk into fine powder | burning a piece of paper to ash | water evaporating from a hot plate | dissolving a spoon of salt in water |
| observation | the powder still tastes and behaves like chalk | only ash and smoke remain | the water seems to disappear completely | the water tastes salty, so the salt is still present |
tables: {"headers":["","W","X","Y","Z"],"rows":[["activity","grinding a piece of chalk into fine powder","burning a piece of paper to ash","water evaporating from a hot plate","dissolving a spoon of salt in water"],["observation","the powder still behaves like chalk","only ash and smoke remain","the water seems to disappear completely","the water tastes salty, so the salt is still present"]],"row_labels":["activity","observation"],"caption":""}

teacher.key_rationale: Grinding chalk (W) and dissolving salt (Z) are physical changes where the substance remains present as extremely small particles even though it is less visible, showing matter does not become nothing. Burning paper (X) is a chemical change producing new substances, and evaporation (Y) as described gives no direct observation that the water still exists, so the pair is W and Z, option B.
